figures.shows: Four quantum circuit templates: (a) a linear QNN with data encoding gates U(x) then variational gates V(theta) then measurements; (b) a linear quantum kernel method with U(x_i) then U-dagger(x_j); (c) a non-linear data re-uploading classifier (QDRC) with alternating U(x) and V(theta); (d) a non-linear QCNN with mid-circuit measurements and measurement-controlled gates W. A dashed red box marks that all models in (a) are contained in (b).
figures.confirmed_by: If data encoding (blue) is separable from variational gates (orange), then the quantum model is linear.

figures.shows: Data encoding strategies, circuit size (qubits) and depth (runtime) for a data vector of dimension d, N samples and tau bits per element: angle encoding O(d) qubits and O(1) depth; basis encoding O(d tau) qubits and O(1) or O(N d tau) depth; amplitude encoding O(log2(d tau)) qubits and O(log2(N d tau)) or O(N d tau) depth; QRAM O(d tau + m) qubits and O(log(m)) depth with m = O(d tau); parallel unary loader O(sqrt(d)) qubits and O(sqrt(d) log2(d)) depth.
figures.confirmed_by: As an example from Fig. 2, angle-encoding can be prepared in constant depth but scales linearly with number of qubits.

figures.shows: The search strategy in the SPICE framework: columns for Setting and Perspective (digital health data terms, joined by OR), Intervention (quantum terms), Comparison (machine learning terms) and Evaluation (date 2015 onward, excluding reviews, protocols and case reports), with the PubMed MeSH query shown in full.
figures.confirmed_by: Search concepts within columns are combined with logical ‘OR’ statements, while independent columns are concatenated with logical ‘AND’ statements.

figures.shows: Eligibility criteria as inclusion and exclusion lists by SPICE element; exclusions include textual or handwritten data in EHRs, quantum-inspired algorithms, quantum sensing, cryptography and key distribution, quantum chemistry and biology calculations, and non-digital-health applications.

papers.what_it_is: A PRISMA systematic review of quantum machine learning for digital health data (2015 to June 2024) that screens 4915 studies, appraises technical rigor, and synthesizes 16 studies with realistic operating conditions.

existing.note: The Conclusion (p.18) and Section 4.2 (p.14) both state it; the authors base it on the 16 synthesized studies, of which five give too little information to compare and eleven show major comparison problems (no scaling, no error bars, no noise characterization).
Fig. 5 on p.10 gives the same flow: 4915 screened, 313 full-text, 169 extracted, 123 low quality, 46 assessed for realistic operating conditions, 30 using only ideal simulations, 16 synthesized.

can access ≈ 1000 qubits, which is an order of magnitude larger than O(100) qubit processors for universal non-annealing quantum computers developed by IBM and Google.

relying solely on ideal simulations offer no insight into robustness

Of eligible studies, we appraise study quality yielding 16 robust studies which analyze QML applications in realistic operating environments.

Our work is the first systematic review that examines the strength of empirical evidence to support these claims using a database of 4915 studies.

existing.value: The saved Gurobi Parameter Reference documents that the MIP solver terminates with an optimal result when the gap between the lower and upper objective bound is less than MIPGap (default 1e-4) times the absolute value of the incumbent objective value, with the gap defined as |z_P - z_D| / |z_P| for primal bound z_P (the incumbent, the upper bound when minimizing) and dual bound z_D; if both bounds are zero the gap is defined to be zero, and if z_P is zero and z_D is not the gap is defined to be infinity; for most models the gap decreases monotonically, but when z_P and z_D have opposite signs the relative gap may increase after a new incumbent although the absolute gap decreased; it also terminates when the gap is less than MIPGapAbs (default 1e-10); both only affect MIP models.

papers.what_it_is: A method that uses a classical approximate simulator (sparse wave function or MPS) to compute a Hessian and conjugate directions for a noise-robust line-search optimizer of VQE circuits, compared with Powell and other optimizers on simulated molecules and run once on ibm_brisbane for a 40-site transverse Ising model.

existing.note: Appendix E.2 adds that the converged QPU result is within 10% of the expected ansatz minimum, and Fig. 4 shows a QPU relative energy error of about 0.08 at iteration 3. The surrogate was an MPS simulator with an artificially small bond dimension of 4, though the ansatz is classically tractable at bond dimension 100 (entered as a new assertion).

papers.what_it_is: A supervised hybrid quantum-classical (parallel FiLM) neural network trained to imitate node-wise Dijkstra routing on one simulated earthquake evacuation graph, with a simulator comparison to a classical network, a three-decision run on IonQ Aria 1, and ZX, Fourier and Fisher analyses of a reduced circuit.

The text states the classical NN arrival rate as 95%, but Fig. 4(a) labels 92% for the classical NN predicting a path and 95% for the HQNN; the value does not state an arrival rate. The paper gives no repeat runs, seeds or test-set size for these averages.

quotes: In this example, the trainable parameter labeled ‘θ8’ – corresponding to RX rotation applied to the first qubit in the final U (θ) layer – is not present as it self-annihilates with its adjoint and thus has no effect on the model output.

assertions.value: The authors report that the frequency of Fisher eigenvalues close to zero increases from 46% for N = 1 repetition and K = 1 reuploading to nearly 65% for N = 2 repetitions and K = 3 reuploadings, and conclude that eigenvalues near zero become more likely as the number of trainable parameters rises.

Nonetheless, even networks with nondegenerate Fisher matrices can suffer from low trainability if a significant proportion of eigenvalues have small absolute values.

as well as the increased expressivity and decreased trainability of the model as the BEL sub-layers increase.
